 p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text" data-subscriber-content> After this week’s major wins by the Democratic Party in the midterm elections, it’s no surprise that the cold open on “Saturday Night Live” was political in nature.
 But there was one surprise guest: The new senator-elect of Texas, James Talarico .
 The cold open began with a conversation between Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (Kenan Thompson) and Sen. Chuck Schumer (Sarah Sherman), the minority leaders of the House and Senate (and possible future majority leaders), respectively, as they celebrated their party’s victory, including flipping Texas blue — for which they took credit. (Schumer: “That was all me. I found the candidates, I recruited them. And as a show of respect, they begged me not to appear at their campaign events.”) 
 Hollywood Inc. 
 Jimmy Kimmel interview with Senate candidate James Talarico won’t air on ABC 
 The comedian’s Thursday interview with the Texas Democrat will play on YouTube rather than on television “out of consideration for our ... ABC affiliates in Texas who would have to deal with this nonsense,” Kimmel said.
 Sept. 10, 2026 Jeffries pledged that their first order of business would be to march up to President Trump and tell him, “Hey, knock it off, Buster.”
 Advertisement But Trump (James Austin Johnson), not one to be left out, interrupted to take the credit for the Democratic victories instead — thanks to the “horrible economy and terrible war.” “So in the words of Moana’s big fat friend, ‘You’re welcome,’” he said.
 After an appearance from JD Vance (Jeremy Culhane) and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth (Colin Jost), plus Trump’s complaints about having to work with millennials and the return of their optimism, he began listing some of the newly elected senators who would be arriving in Washington: “Jon Ossoff, or as I call him Thinky Herman. Abdul El-Sayed, or as I call him, Mamdani for men. And of course, down in Texas, Talafreako.” Talarico then stepped into frame to a roar of applause and cheers from the audience, leading to this exchange:
 × Talarico: “Hi, America, I am James Talarico, the guy who has been texting you every day asking for $5.”
 Advertisement Trump: “In this economy, who can blame you.”
 Talarico: “But I think Mr. President, if we can work together, we can make life better for everyday Americans. It’s clear people want something new. They want something different. I’m talking of course about ‘SNL’s’ cold opens. How many of these Trump freezes are they going to do?”
 Trump: “Infinity.”
 Talarico: “Well in that case, there is only one thing to say: Live from New York, it’s Saturday Night Live.”
 Hollywood Inc. 
 Stephen Colbert escalates dispute with CBS over Talarico interview ban 
 The “Late Show” host said the CBS claim that a U.S. Senate candidate interview was not banned is “crap.”
 Feb. 18, 2026 It’s a notable moment for Talarico and “SNL,” which had shied away from having any cameos from politicians in the the run-up to the midterms like in previous election cycles (former Vice President and Democratic nominee Kamala Harris and GOP candidate Nikki Haley made appearances during the 2024 presidential campaign). For Talarico, it marked the first time he was on a late-night network TV show since embarking on his Senate campaign. Prior attempts to appear for interviews on “ The Late Show With Stephen Colbert ” and “ Jimmy Kimmel Live! ” were stymied by CBS’ and ABC’s executives and lawyers, who cited threats by the FCC, led by chairman Brendan Carr, regarding the equal-time rule , which requires broadcasters to provide equal access to competing political candidates. In the past, daytime and late-night shows weren’t considered subject to the rule, but Carr has said differently. The issue also arose after Harris’ “SNL” appearance . (Talarico’s interviews with Colbert and Kimmel ended up on their show’s YouTube accounts.)
 Hollywood Inc. 
 Trump campaign gets equal time from NBC after Harris’ ‘SNL’ appearance 
 Trump received free one-minute spots during NASCAR and ‘Sunday Night Football’ after Harris’ sketch on ‘SNL.’
 Nov. 4, 2024 Trump has been a vocal critic of the late-night show hosts and “SNL” over the course of his tenure as president. While Talarico has called out Trump and his administration’s policies in the past, his message on Saturday was much more conciliatory. Whether Trump accepts the olive branch remains to be seen.
